key_insight: Human–machine interactions at multiple points in the AI life cycle shape the degree of meaningful human control in military systems; governance must address design, deployment, and oversight together rather than treating control as a single operational setting.
problem_solved: Clarifies how interactions across design, testing, deployment, and feedback loops create governance gaps that undermine accountable human decision‑making in military AI.
method: Conceptual mapping of human–machine interaction points across the AI life cycle (design → testing → deployment → monitoring).
Analytic examination of how those interaction patterns affect human control, responsibility, and decision quality in military contexts.
Policy-focused synthesis offering governance levers and principles to align technical design with legal, ethical, and operational accountability.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners and policy makers recognize where technical design choices translate into governance risks, enabling more responsible system design and clearer accountability pathways in high‑stakes military applications.
visual_elements: AI life‑cycle diagram highlighting human interaction nodes (design, validation, deployment, monitoring)
Comparison chart illustrating modes of control (human-in-the-loop, on-the-loop, out-of-the-loop) and their governance implications
Risk vs. oversight matrix showing where governance gaps commonly occur and suggested interventions
Icon set: engineer/designer, commander/decision-maker, autonomous system, regulatory/policy shield
paper_title: Re-thinking human–machine interaction and the governance of AI in the military domain
